blocks.x: IoT, Twin & Robotics applied to K-12 & School Systems. This page sets out the operating context, the delivery pattern we run, the services and platforms involved, and the outcomes we commit to.

School systems serve every child under public scrutiny: learning analytics, special-education compliance, safeguarding and parental communication. Technology must be privacy-strict (minors), accessibility-complete and teacher-time-respecting.

items: Energy and space unmanaged across school estates.
Assessment, attendance and wellbeing data siloed; interventions late.

blocks.x: The pattern composes Robotics & Autonomous Systems Integration, Smart Infrastructure, Buildings & Cities, Computer Vision & Edge AI from the IoT, Digital Twin & Robotics tower, wired into the unit's workflows (Learning analytics, Safeguarding case management, Special-ed compliance) on Dataq Twinverse and Dataq Nexus. Governance inherits the sector frame — FERPA/GDPR-K among others — with evidence generated by the delivery itself.

items: Facilities that run themselves: BMS/IoT fusion, energy optimization and city-scale platforms.
Sense everything that matters: retrofit-friendly sensor network with governed telemetry.
Simulate before you cut steel: plant, fleet and product twins with governed physics and data.

At Education & Research level this capability reads as: freezer/ventilation monitoring with alerting (research asset loss prevented). The sub-industry page narrows it to the unit's workflows, regimes and KPIs.

The engagement cadence below is the standard pattern for this capability. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
